clue.text: Charming employer of noteworthy apprentice

parts.note: one who works charms and spells, and whose famous trainee features in Goethe's ballad and Dukas's music

explanation.surface: Praise for a delightful boss who took on a gifted trainee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charming' reads as 'delightful' but means 'casting charms'; the 'noteworthy apprentice' is the one in Dukas's piece, noteworthy because it is music.
explanation.definitionFit: A wizard who casts spells employed the apprentice in the famous tale of the brooms.

clue.text: Introduction to plain and river

parts.note: overt means plain or open to view
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: An opening passage describing flat land and a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like the flat landscape noun, but it is the adjective meaning obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestral prelude opens an opera, and the word also means an opening approach.

clue.text: Vulgar prosperity of a league of nations

parts.note: common means coarse or vulgar
wealth is prosperity

explanation.surface: Crude riches belonging to an international alliance.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain and its former colonies form a voluntary association of countries.

clue.text: Songster finds Communist, emblem sort of square

parts.note: red is the colour and nickname of communists
a star is an emblem, as on a Soviet flag
a T-square is a drafting tool

explanation.surface: A singer discovers a communist, a badge and a kind of plaza.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Songster' is a songbird; the red star was the Soviet emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: A small thrush-like bird with an orange tail is a singer of the woods.

clue.text: Underdone portion of regional dish

parts.note: rare meat is lightly cooked
a bit is a small portion

explanation.surface: Part of a local speciality has been undercooked.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh rarebit is cheese on toast, named for Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh cheese melted on toast is a speciality associated with one part of Britain.

clue.text: Rogue in US Intelligence is a six-footer

indicators.note: in places the rogue inside the American spy agency

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency
a cad is a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: A scoundrel in American spying circles is a very tall man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' suggests a tall person, but an insect has six feet.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect, which has six legs, famous for its loud summer chirping.

clue.text: Something fishy about Henry's wife?

explanation.surface: A suspicion concerning the spouse of King Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something fishy' suggests a suspicious matter, but it is literally a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A young salmon in its river stage, and Catherine, the sixth and last queen of Henry VIII.

clue.text: County altered date for supporting the retired

parts.note: Beds is short for Bedfordshire, an English county

indicators.note: altered means changed, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A county council changed the date for funding pensioners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altered' makes TEAD from DATE; 'the retired' are not pensioners but people who have gone to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed's frame holds up those who have turned in for the night.

clue.text: Right, in a goddess, to produce 18

indicators.note: the word in tells us the legal right sits inside the a-plus-goddess pair

parts.note: Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin
a lien is a legal right to hold property against a debt

explanation.surface: Granting a claim to a deity somehow causes ill feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is the answer to 18 down, AVERSION; to make someone feel aversion is to estrange them.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange someone is to turn them against you, creating dislike or aversion.

clue.text: Instructive time for Hilary, say

explanation.surface: A teaching period named after somebody called Hilary.
explanation.walkthrough: Hilary is not a person but the spring session of the law courts and Oxford University.
explanation.definitionFit: A school or university session is a period of teaching; Hilary is the name of the Oxford and legal session after Christmas.

clue.text: Eg Melville's Claggart, ruined by a tar's stammer

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked and reshaped, so the following letters are jumbled

parts.note: the S of the possessive counts here as a letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A villain in Billy Budd is undone by a sailor's stutter.
explanation.walkthrough: John Claggart is the ship's police officer in Herman Melville's Billy Budd; fittingly, Billy himself has a stammer and is a tar.
explanation.definitionFit: Claggart holds the naval rank of chief disciplinary petty officer aboard the warship in Melville's novella.

clue.text: Joint act of speaking

explanation.surface: A shared performance of speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' reads as 'shared' but is the noun, a hinge between bones.
explanation.definitionFit: A movable connection between parts, as in a skeleton, and clear pronunciation of speech.

clue.text: Money for land in Africa

explanation.surface: Funds raised for territory on the African continent.
explanation.definitionFit: An old British gold coin worth 21 shillings, and also a West African country.

clue.text: Uninvolved in part 'of play I've written

parts.note: a play is divided into acts
the contraction I've written out as letters

explanation.surface: Someone stays detached from a role in a play they have authored.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray quote mark is OCR noise; the page reads 'in part of play I've written'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone idle or not taking part is not involved in what is happening.

clue.text: In a manner unworthy of egghead born in Bath

indicators.note: the word in places the egg's head and born inside the city name

parts.note: the English spa city, taken as written
the head of the word egg is its first letter, E
née, French for born, is used of a woman's maiden name

explanation.surface: A clever person born in the city of Bath is thought unworthy of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egghead' looks like a brainy person, but it is just the head of 'egg', E.
explanation.definitionFit: A task that is below your dignity is one you consider unworthy of you.

clue.text: Couple permitted to identify jewelry item

parts.note: a brace is a pair
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A pair are allowed to pick out a piece of jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A band worn round the wrist as an ornament.

clue.text: First murderer involved in useless Pope's work

indicators.note: in places the shuffled murderer inside the word for useless

parts.note: a dud is something that does not work

indicators.note: involved means twisted or tangled, so the name's letters are mixed

parts.note: Cain, who killed Abel, is the Bible's first murderer

explanation.surface: Cain somehow implicated in a worthless papal document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pope' is not the pontiff but Alexander Pope, the 18th-century poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Pope's mock-epic satire on dullness and bad writers is titled with this name.

clue.text: It's upheld as protection against downfall'

definitions.text: It's upheld as protection against downfall'

parts.words: It's upheld as protection against downfall'
parts.note: held up overhead to keep off falling rain, with downfall read as a shower

explanation.surface: Something maintained to prevent a person's ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Downfall' suggests ruin but means rain falling down; the stray quote mark is OCR noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A folding canopy held over the head shelters against rain.

clue.text: Object of dislike is about to turn up in county

indicators.note: in places the turned pair inside the county name

parts.note: Avon was an English county around Bristol

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Something hated is about to appear in the shires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn up' turns the pair to give ERSI; Avon was a county from 1974 to 1996, so the clue relies on a now-abolished name.
explanation.definitionFit: Something you strongly dislike is a pet hate.

clue.text: Not' prepared to be like Edgar's son

explanation.surface: Someone is not ready to resemble the son of Edgar.
explanation.walkthrough: Ethelred the Unready, son of King Edgar, was an English king around 1000; the stray quote mark is OCR noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking readiness, and the epithet of Ethelred, the Anglo-Saxon king whose father was Edgar.

clue.text: Fisher, without hesitation, I can denominate thus

indicators.note: without tells us the sound of hesitation is dropped from the fisherman

parts.note: an angler fishes with rod and line
er is the sound of hesitating in speech
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fisherman, without pausing, says he can name something this way.
explanation.walkthrough: Geoffrey Fisher was Archbishop of Canterbury, so 'Fisher' also hints at the church in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The Church of England's denomination is the one to which this name applies.

clue.text: Spoken after church? No, sung

indicators.note: after puts the spoken word behind the church abbreviation

parts.note: oral means spoken

explanation.surface: A question about speech after a service, answered with singing.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'No' makes the surface a contradiction while the definition sits at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Music for a choir is performed by voices together.

clue.text: Is this missile in the news summary?

definitions.text: Is this missile in the news summary?

parts.words: Is this missile in the news summary?
parts.note: the projectile from a gun shares its name with the dot marking each point in a list of headlines

explanation.surface: Asking whether a rocket attack featured in the headlines.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun's projectile, and also the typographic dot that heads each point in a summary list.

clue.text: See installation

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese, and a new bishop is installed by being seated on the throne

explanation.surface: A notice inviting people to look at an art exhibit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb, look, but it is the noun for a bishop's area of authority.
explanation.definitionFit: The ceremony of placing a monarch or bishop on the throne is formal installation in office.

clue.text: River pilot — sort of

explanation.surface: A river navigator of a kind.
explanation.walkthrough: The Test is a Hampshire river famous for trout; a pilot is a trial run.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hampshire chalk stream, and a trial, of which a pilot study is one kind.

clue.text: One bird's lost its way — this one?

definitions.text: One bird's lost its way — this one?

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: lost its tells us the road abbreviation drops out of the word for bird

parts.note: the possessive read as plural, birds
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A wondering question about which kind of bird has gone astray.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing RD from BIRDS leaves BIS, and the whole clue describes a wading bird as well.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-billed wading bird, sacred in ancient Egypt, is the one that has wandered.

clue.text: "By the old Moulmein Pagoda, Lookin' — to the sea" (Kipling)

definitions.text: "By the old Moulmein Pagoda, Lookin' — to the sea" (Kipling)

parts.words: "By the old Moulmein Pagoda, Lookin' — to the sea" (Kipling)
parts.note: the missing word comes from the opening of Kipling's poem Mandalay, giving a compass direction toward the sunrise

explanation.surface: A gap-fill from a famous Kipling poem set in Burma.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening lines of Kipling's Mandalay; Moulmein is a Burmese port, and the girl looks toward the sea from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Facing toward the direction of sunrise, which is how the Burmese girl looks out to sea in the poem.

clue.text: Strong desire of youth leader in paid employment

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, so take the start of youth

parts.note: someone earning is working for money

explanation.surface: A young person's ambition to get a paid job.
explanation.definitionFit: Longing is a powerful wish for something out of reach.
